## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 58, titled *Dubbaṇṇakaraṇa* ("Not making stains on a new robe"), establishes that a monk incurs an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) if he wears a newly obtained robe without first marking or disfiguring it [SuttaCentral; Radich 2007; Horner]. In the text's origin story (*vatthu*, Vin IV 120), a group of monks traveling between Sāketa and Sāvatthī are robbed alongside wandering ascetics (*paribbājaka*); when the king's men recapture the stolen property, the monks are unable to distinguish their own robes from those of the ascetics [Bechert, Bretfeld, and Kieffer-Pülz 1997; Rosen 1959]. The rule stipulates that a new robe is one that has not yet been rendered allowable (*akatakappa*) [Hüsken 1997]. As explained in the commentary (*Samantapāsādikā* 863), making the robe allowable (*kappakaraṇa*) requires dyeing it and applying an identification mark, such as a colored smudge on one corner [Horner; Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral confirm that this rule exists across the Vinaya literature of nearly all early Buddhist schools, including the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Pātimokkhas of the Sarvāstivāda (Pc 59), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Pc 58), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 77), Mahāsāṃghika (Pc 48), and Dharmaguptaka (Pc 60) traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral; Rosen 1959]. Automated alignments by DharmaNexus reflect this cross-linguistic agreement, finding matches in the Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* and Tibetan Vinayavibhaṅga (*’Dul ba rnam par ’byed pa*, D0003-3) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali Canon, DharmaNexus detects 280 shared passages across 53 texts, identifying significant formulaic overlap with Khandhaka chapters such as the *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15), *Vattakkhandhaka* (Kd 18), and *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), as well as neighboring Vibhaṅga rules like Pācittiya 59 [DharmaNexus].
